title: PulseShift: Calibrated Forecasting of Weather-Driven Mobility Suppression and Hourly Identification of Air-Quality Effects
description: A calibrated, decision-focused forecast of whether weather and air quality suppress an outdoor session in Washington DC, where the outcome is outdoor mobility proxied by bike-share ridership. An identification analysis shows that the daily air-quality–mobility association is largely seasonal confounding and that hourly, within-day data is needed to correct it. Includes a reproducible Python pipeline and a zero-dependency browser app.
